Romansh was elevated to the status of a national language (alongside German, French, and Italian) through a popular vote in **1996**.  

Since the revision of the language article in the Swiss Constitution in 1996, Romansh is recognized as **one of Switzerland's four national languages** with official status at the federal level. This means it is used in certain official communications and has specific rights and protections in areas where Romansh-speaking communities reside.
